Jennifer —

Thanks for the clear redlines and the heads up. Quick answers up front, then I’ll outline a proposal:

- Baseline: We can consider 99.95% as a committed availability anchor for the Aurora clinical ingestion cluster, provided Aurora agrees to a narrow operational carveout for scheduled maintenance windows and an annual ingress capacity test window.

- Earnback: We’re open to a staged earnback approach tied to remediation timelines and RCA acceptance. Proposal below.

Proposal (summary):
- Committed baseline: 99.95% monthly availability for the scoped endpoints.
- Remedy structure: Monthly credit pool calculated as percentage of monthly bill, capped at 20%.
- Earnback path: Up to 50% of credited amount may be earned back within the following 60 days if:
    * Redwood completes remediation milestones in agreed timeframe (timeline in attachment), and
    * Aurora accepts RCA and runbook updates within 10 business days.
- Incident reporting & SLA measurement: daily incident digest + tokenized latency p95 reporting; measurement window aligns to UTC calendar month.

I’ve attached a redline of our suggested wording and a short runbook milestone table. If that direction looks reasonable, I can send a formal amendment for legal review and loop in Contracts.

Available tomorrow 2–4pm PT for a call; happy to take a preferred time.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise

Subject: Internal: Aurora SLA questions — proposed legal language and limits

Team — notes from the call with Aurora (recap for our counsel):

1) Scope: narrow to production ingestion and realtime annotate endpoints in us-west-2.
2) Baseline uplift: approve conditional 99.95% anchor with the following guardrails:
   - Maintenance carveout: up to 6 hours/month scheduled (2x 3-hour windows), 7 days’ notice; emergency maintenance excluded but limited.
   - Capacity test carveout: one planned ingress test per year (up to 4 hours).
3) Remedy & earnback: accept staged earnback model but cap total earnback at 50% of credited amount and limit overall monthly credit cap to 20% of invoice.
4) RCA acceptance: Aurora must provide written acceptance or a list of objections within 10 business days to trigger earnback release.

Noting legal wants explicit phrasing around measurement (UTC month, source of truth: Redwood metrics dashboard + joint audit right once/year). Also request that any DocuSign amendment reference deal AH-2027-74.

I’ll draft the redline to send to Ben for pricing confirmation and then to Marissa for external send.

—Laura
Sr. Counsel, Contracts

Jennifer/Samir —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the thoughtful questions. Per our call and internal review, Redwood can commit to the following amendment (high level):

- Scope: production ingestion.* and realtime-annotate.* APIs, region: us-west-2.
- Availability commitment: 99.95% monthly uptime (UTC calendar month), with measurement from Redwood's metrics as the operational source of truth.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (up to 6 hours/month, 7 days’ notice) and one annual ingress capacity test (up to 4 hours).
- Remedy: monthly credit pool = min(20% of monthly invoice, calculated per current formula).
- Earnback: up to 50% of credited amount may be returned to Redwood within 60 days if Redwood: (a) completes remediation milestones in agreed times, and (b) Aurora provides written RCA acceptance within 10 business days.
- Audit: joint audit right once per 12 months limited to SLA measurement data.

Next steps: Laura will send a redline amendment referencing AH-2027-74 and I’ll include the pricing addendum to reflect the uplifted commitment (small monthly uplift to cover increased SLO). If Aurora is good with this, please confirm and we’ll route to DocuSign by end of next week.

Appreciate the collaboration — I’ll open the DocuSign envelope once I get the greenlight.

Best,
Marissa
